title: Regular domain divisor quotient of canonical strict henselization
statement: Let R be regular, R/(f) regular, and b(f) nonunit at a geometric point. The divisor quotient of the canonical strict henselization is regular and a domain.

source.place: Tag 0EYG (pione-lemma-abhyankar-one-divisor), strict henselization paragraph; Tag 05WS (lemma-quotient-strict-henselization); Tag 06LN, regularity under strict henselization.

proof.text: Identify the small and full affine-neighbourhood colimits using smallStrictHenselizationColimitIso. The final-functor coprojection formula and the defining structural-map equations show that Spec of the comparison followed by the small structural map is strictLocalizationToBase. Compose b with the comparison; its inverse preserves the nonunit hypothesis. Apply the retained upstream regularity component to this composite. Ideal.quotientEquiv for the inverse comparison identifies the two principal quotients, and IsRegularRing.of_ringEquiv transports regularity back to the original small-colimit quotient. Pair this regularity proof with the unchanged domain component to obtain the conjunction.

lean.statement:
theorem strictHenselizationRing_regular_divisor_quotient
    (R : CommRingCat.{u}) [IsRegularRing R] (f : R)
    [IsRegularRing (R ⧸ Ideal.span {f})]
    {Ω : Type u} [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω]
    (barY : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ Spec R)
    (b : R ⟶ strictHenselizationRing barY)
    (hb : Spec.map b = strictHenselizationStructuralMap barY)
    (hg : ¬ IsUnit (b.hom f)) :
    IsRegularRing (strictHenselizationRing barY ⧸ Ideal.span {b.hom f}) ∧
      IsDomain (strictHenselizationRing barY ⧸ Ideal.span {b.hom f})
